question: Identify the artist with the highest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order) and the artist with the lowest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order), then calculate the amount each customer spent specifically on those two artists’ albums. Next, compute the average spending for the customers who purchased from the top-selling artist and the average spending for the customers who purchased from the lowest-selling artist, and finally return the absolute difference between these two averages.
sql:
-- Calculate average spending for each artist's customers and the absolute difference
WITH artist_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        a.Name as artist_name,
        SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) as total_sales
    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
    JOIN artists a ON al.ArtistId = a.ArtistId
    GROUP BY a.Name
),
top_artist AS (
    SELECT artist_name FROM artist_sales ORDER BY total_sales DESC, artist_name ASC LIMIT 1
),
bottom_artist AS (
    SELECT artist_name FROM artist_sales ORDER BY total_sales ASC, artist_name ASC LIMIT 1
),
customer_spending AS (
    SELECT 
        ar.Name as artist_name,
        c.CustomerId,
        SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) as spending
    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN invoices inv ON ii.InvoiceId = inv.InvoiceId
    JOIN customers c ON inv.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
    JOIN artists ar ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
    WHERE ar.Name IN (
        (SELECT artist_name FROM top_artist),
        (SELECT artist_name FROM bottom_artist)
    )
    GROUP BY ar.Name, c.CustomerId
),
avg_spending AS (
    SELECT 
        artist_name,
        AVG(spending) as avg_spending
    FROM customer_spending
    GROUP BY artist_name
)
SELECT 
    (SELECT avg_spending FROM avg_spending WHERE artist_name = (SELECT artist_name FROM top_artist)) as top_artist_avg,
    (SELECT avg_spending FROM avg_spending WHERE artist_name = (SELECT artist_name FROM bottom_artist)) as bottom_artist_avg,
    ABS((SELECT avg_spending FROM avg_spending WHERE artist_name = (SELECT artist_name FROM top_artist)) - 
        (SELECT avg_spending FROM avg_spending WHERE artist_name = (SELECT artist_name FROM bottom_artist))) as absolute_difference

The main transactional tables are invoices and invoice_items, which record sales events. Invoices link to customers via CustomerId, while invoice_items connect invoices to specific tracks using InvoiceId and TrackId respectively. The tracks table serves as the central entity for media content, linking to albums, genres, and media types through AlbumId, GenreId, and MediaTypeId. {"sql": "-- Calculate average spending for each artist's customers and the absolute difference
WITH artist_sales AS (

    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId

    JOIN artists a ON al.ArtistId = a.ArtistId
    GROUP BY a.Name
),
top_artist AS (
    SELECT artist_name FROM artist_sales ORDER BY total_sales DESC, artist_name ASC LIMIT 1
),
bottom_artist AS (
    SELECT artist_name FROM artist_sales ORDER BY total_sales ASC, artist_name ASC LIMIT 1
),
customer_spending AS (
    SELECT 
        ar.Name as artist_name,
        c.CustomerId,
        SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) as spending
    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN invoices inv ON ii.InvoiceId = inv.InvoiceId
    JOIN customers c ON inv.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
    JOIN artists ar ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
    WHERE ar.Name IN (

),
avg_spending AS (

)
